thread:
alex.g: heads-up — saw a weird kv cache correctness signal in prod canary. tokens from previous request occasionally reappearing in new responses when context length crosses ~32k tokens. reproduces on a local stress run with batch mixing enabled.

maya_r: ugh. is that the alignment bug or something else? any logs? :thinking_face:

alex.g: initial log excerpt:```
KVPageManager: alloc page=0x7f8b3f00 size=65536 seq=4821 req=0x1a7f
KVPageManager: evict page=0x7f8b100 seq=3189 req=0x19ff free_list_push idx=4
KVCache: reuse page=0x7f8b100 seq=4821 req=0x1a7f
```
You can see the same page address reused for a different seq id without zeroing the tail region. When new request is shorter than previous occupant, old tail tokens leak into output (non-deterministic).

samir: that log suggests freelist reuse without clearing or proper boundary enforcement. do we track page.owner_request_id on reuse?

alex.g: not currently — we have `seq` and `last_used_ts`, but no strong per-request fencing. code path is this: allocate -> evict asynchronously -> push to freelist -> pop for next allocation. race window if eviction completes while pop occurs for another request.

maya_r: does this only happen with batching enabled? could be mixing requests inside same worker and not resetting KV slot offsets.

alex.g: batching + very long contexts + prefetching seems to increase probability. stress script attached in gist (link).

leah: repro steps? I can run an isolated binary against a debug build.

alex.g: steps:
1) run perf_stress --mix-batches --max-context=65536 --qps=100
2) send seed prompt A (20k tokens) then B (2k tokens) rapidly
3) inspect generated tokens for substrings from A in B

I have a minimized test that hits it ~1/200 runs.

samir: quick triage idea — add a `owner_seq` tag to page headers and assert on reuse if owner_seq != requested_seq in debug builds. That should fail fast. Also zero out tail when evicting/repurposing.

alex.g: agreed. also suspect off-by-one in allocation alignment when page spans aren't multiple of block_size. If we split blocks across a page boundary, reclaim code wasn't adjusting the in-page offsets. That could leave partial KV-blocks from previous seq inline.

maya_r: can you paste the allocation snippet?

alex.g:```
// simplified
if (page->free_offset + alloc_size <= PAGE_SIZE) {
  // use here
  ptr = page->base + page->free_offset;
  page->free_offset += alloc_size;
} else {
  // fallback to freelist
}
```
We don't check `page->owner_seq` and we don't round alloc_size up to block alignment in a few hot paths.

samir: ok. next steps:
- add owner_seq metadata
- enforce block alignment on all alloc paths
- zero tail region on evict
- add a stress-only sanitizer that randomizes page reuse timing and asserts no cross-request bytes visible
- roll a debug canary build to prod canary (and keep telemetry)

leah: I can PR the owner_seq assert + zeroing today. patch will be small.

alex.g: thanks. also we should add a perf test to measure the cost of zeroing. if it's too heavy, consider selective zero (only tail region > used_len) and a lightweight fingerprint check instead of full zeroing.

maya_r: fingerprinting (e.g., 64-bit checksum) might be faster. on reuse, compare stored checksum to expected (but you'd need to compute expected after full zeroing once...). might get complicated.

samir: or we do a hybrid: for normal path, zero only the tail bytes that could be observed by the next request; for paranoid debug builds, do full zero. That keeps perf hit minimal.

ci-bot: CI: test_kv_freelist_debug failing on linux-release-x64 (timeout). Link: https://ci.example/1234

alex.g: that CI failure is unrelated — flaky test. ignore for now.

deploy-bot: canary deploy queued: build/redwood/kvpatch-1769 -> env/canary (manual approval required).

maya_r: once patch lands, let's add an e2e that simulates mixed long+short contexts with batching on/off and assert no cross-token contamination. Also add perf dashboard to track p50/p95 mem growth for long contexts.

leah: PR opened: https://git.example/r/infra/+/3456 — implements owner_seq and zero-tail, adds unit + stress test.

alex.g: code looks good. can we get an extra reviewer on the eviction race path? @samir ?

samir: reviewing now. initial comment: move the zeroing into the evict path (so freelist always receives zeroed pages) to minimize scattered zero ops during alloc. also add a fast-path that marks page as "clean" when we know whole page was overwritten.

leah: updated. pushed new commit with evict-path-zeroing and a `page->clean` flag.

deploy-bot: canary deploy started: canary-2026-03-17-02. monitor: infra/perf/kv-leaks.

alex.g: monitoring shows 0 occurrences in canary so far (2h). stress harness on debug build shows fail-rate dropped from 1/200 to 0/1000. promising.

maya_r: plan: backport to stable branch, add automated e2e for mixed contexts, and keep the telemetry dash (alert if >0 contamination events per 1M requests). I'll file the follow-ups.

samir: file created: https://triage.example/issue/RED-889 (kv freelist cross-request contamination). assign to infra.

alex.g: thanks everyone. we'll keep this thread for rollout notes and ETA for backport.

leah: note for postmortem template: include root cause = freelist reuse + lack of owner fencing + partial-block alignment bug causing stale tail bytes. mitigation = eviction zeroing + owner_seq fencing + alignment enforcement.

maya_r: :white_check_mark: set. closing monitoring loop after next minor release.
